# Pre-registered rubric
Each event receives independent columns: target semantic pass, exact typed operation match (unordered operations unless dependency makes order material), expected status/reason, full state and projection equality, backend invariant preservation, retrieval calls/bytes and total visible input/output bytes. Target prose must meaningfully render museum/display/custody as seed/garden/planting, retain intended identity, requested dates/notes/approval distinctions and atomicity where material, avoid claiming confirmed host success, and preserve rejection or genuine ambiguity. Equivalent target prose is accepted; field names alone are insufficient. Notes must be exact in typed operations. Ambiguity requires clarification with no mutation. Generic prose omitting a material constraint fails semantic review even if typed operations are right.

Single continuing 32-event chain, no resets, no model repair, one fresh isolated interpreter per event. Static actor/scope/ID roster/all operation capabilities are identical throughout, not selected from event oracle. Interpreters choose retrieval. Query history includes only completed actual past events. Context focus updates only following a committed single-entity transaction. Failed/malformed output remains observed and chain continues if possible. A divergent input state is flagged as possible cascade; intended oracle and observed outcome remain distinct. Never count runtime rejection alone as interpretation success. No denominator exclusions after seeing results. No correction to backend/oracle after freeze; any discovered design flaw is reported, not relabeled as model failure. Normal API errors are recorded, no hidden repair.

Ancestor rules change only after L23 context issuance, from public deadline Feb28 to Feb01 (all existing due dates remain legal). L24 is a new event with fresh context, not replay. Approval revocation at L21 uses trusted host removal of the unused approval and index rebuild; engine has no public revoke operation. Scope permission persists. It tests supplied-key lookup rejection, not a modeled revoked-token ledger. No claim of sandbox isolation: interpreter constraints are instruction-level.

Freeze backend, fixture, events, expected oracle states/projections, harness, retrieval code, contract and this rubric before first model call. Preserve random context tokens and exact proposals/results in recorded run for reproducibility; replay validates the recorded contexts rather than assuming reproducible random tokens. Child final transcript can be audited separately from response.json. Retrieval bytes count UTF-8 rendered JSON, not hidden model/system tokens; prompt and contract bytes reported separately. No comparative token advantage or generalization rate will be inferred from this one workflow.
